E029 (warm-up halved, −0.21 pp) and E030 (Lookahead every 10 steps, −0.55 pp) both kept the step count and the randint/randperm stream, and both fell. Any change to the training dynamics, even a tiny one, makes the per-seed endpoints diverge, so the tip's +0.2 pp seed luck is lost whether or not the RNG stream is kept. New baseline for any modification to the tip: the 3-seed mean regresses to about 0.7526, then the idea's own effect is added on top, then noise with SD ≈ 0.15 pp on the 3-seed mean. So the bar of 0.753 requires a true gain of at least about +0.05 pp, and nearly every neutral idea now lands at 0.750–0.755.

2. The schedule sits at a sharp local optimum. Weight decay, label smoothing, Muon lr and the averaging ramp all form a flat plateau (E013, E014, E016, E022, E025). The schedule's timing is not flat: the warm-up (E029) and the Lookahead interval (E030, a big loss) are both tuned. Lookahead every 5 steps is load-bearing. Averaging more coarsely loses because the fast weights drift too far between resets while the 64× bias-lr SGD groups are still hot. Prior for any further time-neutral booster: mean effect about −0.05 pp, rarely more than +0.15.

Cutting backward work near the stem pays off far more than its MAC share suggests (E028: −0.84 s). The whitening bias keeps requires_grad=True after step 75 even though its lr is 0, so the full-resolution input-gradient and GELU backward work there is wasted. 6. Noise. A 3-seed re-draw has SD about 0.25 pp per seed, about 0.15 pp on the mean. A rebuild moves the mean by about 0.05 pp. A 10-seed held-out mean has SE about 0.08 pp.

W5 (contrarian), after E030. Tip E027: 8.75 epochs, 219 steps, 20/24/28/32 px at 0/15/40/70% of steps, 5.878 s, 0.7547 on seeds 0–2, about 0.7526 held-out.

1. Revised luck mechanism: chaotic decorrelation. I used to think RNG-preserving tweaks keep the tip's lucky seeds 0–2. E029 (warm-up halved, −0.21 pp) and E030 (Lookahead every 10 steps, −0.55 pp) both kept the step count and the randint/randperm stream, and both fell. Any change to the training dynamics, even a tiny one, makes the per-seed endpoints diverge, so the tip's +0.2 pp seed luck is lost whether or not the RNG stream is kept. New baseline for any modification to the tip: the 3-seed mean regresses to about 0.7526, then the idea's own effect is added on top, then noise with SD ≈ 0.15 pp on the 3-seed mean. So the bar of 0.753 requires a true gain of at least about +0.05 pp, and nearly every neutral idea now lands at 0.750–0.755.

2. The schedule sits at a sharp local optimum. Weight decay, label smoothing, Muon lr and the averaging ramp all form a flat plateau (E013, E014, E016, E022, E025). The schedule's timing is not flat: the warm-up (E029) and the Lookahead interval (E030, a big loss) are both tuned. Lookahead every 5 steps is load-bearing. Averaging more coarsely loses because the fast weights drift too far between resets while the 64× bias-lr SGD groups are still hot. Prior for any further time-neutral booster: mean effect about −0.05 pp, rarely more than +0.15.

3. Time model (I overestimated time repeatedly, so I'm calibrating down). About 23 ms per step on average, roughly 27 ms at 32 px, 21 ms at 24 px and 16–17 ms at 20 px. Converting a 24 px step to 20 px saves about 5.4 ms (E026: 34 steps, −0.18 s). Fixed overhead (prepare plus the first epoch's augmentation) is about 0.5 s. Cutting backward work near the stem pays off far more than its MAC share suggests (E028: −0.84 s). The whitening bias keeps requires_grad=True after step 75 even though its lr is 0, so the full-resolution input-gradient and GELU backward work there is wasted. A second captured graph without it is an untested saving of about 2–4% at identical math (it would still decorrelate the seeds only if the numerics change, and freezing a param with lr 0 doesn't change them).

4. Resolution. Early low resolution is nearly free: E026's held-out mean of 0.7541 matched E016's. Late low resolution, or a big jump into the 32 px tail, costs 0.3–0.9 pp (E011, E018, E024).

5. Epoch dial. Each −0.25 epoch saves about 0.14 s and costs about 0.12 pp. Since the tip's held-out mean is already below 0.753, time can only be cut by bit-identical systems wins or by early-phase resolution cuts that are nearly free.

6. Noise. A 3-seed re-draw has SD about 0.25 pp per seed, about 0.15 pp on the mean. A rebuild moves the mean by about 0.05 pp. A 10-seed held-out mean has SE about 0.08 pp.

Unsure: whether bit-identical systems levers (dropping the whitening-bias grad, fusion) remain; how results transfer to the PCIe judge; whether the 40-seed population mean of about 0.7526 is safe against the 0.75 bar (probably yes).

forecasts.reason: About 9% fewer steps saves about 0.4 s, but dropping the 'easy' samples under LS 0.3 and crop noise is close to a plain epoch cut (≈ −0.4 pp) plus regression from the lucky seeds; it misses the bar.
An abrupt switch of loss scale late in the run, with averaging already forming, gains at most a small amount; seeds decorrelate and regress to about 0.7526.
33 steps go from 24 to 20 px at about 5.4 ms each (≈ −0.17 s); the early phase is almost free, but chaotic regression puts seeds 0–2 near the bar.
GELU/BN/Muon already absorb the stem mismatch, and the 32 px switch still forces re-adaptation; the extra eigh/interpolate in prepare adds about 30–60 ms.

cruxes: Does a dynamics-only change that keeps the RNG stream identical keep the tip's lucky seeds 0–2? Test: rerun the tip with one numerically irrelevant change (e.g. setting requires_grad=False on the whitening bias after step 75, so the math stays bit-identical) and check whether the per-seed accuracies match exactly.
How much time is spent on the full-resolution whitening and group-1 backward after the whitening bias freezes? If it is 3% or more, it is a free time cut that keeps the seed luck.

Is the population mean of the 40-seed PCIe judge for the tip at least 0.751? If so, the 3-seed rule is the binding constraint, and only ideas that keep the per-seed outcomes bit-identical can cut time without first gaining accuracy.
